engagement_title: The Marchfield Exchange sign programme: recover the 1911 house crest from a weathered brass plaque and a faded letterhead, hand the fabricator engraving ready geometry, and rebuild the entrance, directory and suite plates as one editable system
vertical: Real estate and property, a managing agent for a listed 1911 commercial building let to professional firms (Portland, Maine)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post 'Logo Vectorization + Brand Identity Kit' (cands/cand_45.json, db_i 0), whose client has 'an existing logo I love' and needs a designer to 'Vectorize and clean up my current logo to print-ready quality' and 'Build out a full set of logo variations and brand files I can use across everything', listing 'Master logo in vector format', a 'One-color version (white on dark, black on light)' and files 'sized and ready for' named physical applications, and stating 'Please do NOT apply if: You only deliver JPG or PNG files'. Co-anchor: the Upwork post 'Logo Design & Challenge Coin Artwork' (cands/cand_38.json, db_i 95), which asks for artwork 'that can be sent to a mint/manufacturer', insists on 'True vector artwork, not raster images' and requires it be 'Readable at small sizes'. Neither post names a real client; the managing agent, the building, its crest and its tenants are invented here. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the first post's 'exact hex, CMYK, and Pantone codes' and 'Font identification' are not connector work, since nothing here measures a colour or identifies a typeface from an image, so the commission is carried by what is real: recovery of a mark surviving only on physical objects, engraving ready geometry judged against a fabricator's stated minimum stroke, panels authored at true physical sizes as a native editable document, and a per suite plate run built off the previous sign shop's own press artwork.
client_one_liner: We manage a 1911 building whose original house crest survives on a weathered brass plaque by the door and on a fifty year old letterhead, the sign shop needs artwork it can engrave, and fourteen suites need plates that match.
client_brief:
The Marchfield Exchange, sign programme

We are the managing agent for a listed 1911 commercial building in Portland. Fourteen suites, let to law firms, an architecture practice and two accountancy firms, at forty five to seventy five dollars a square foot. The building is the reason tenants take space here, and its sign programme has drifted: a plastic directory board from the nineties, mismatched suite plates from a 2019 refit, and by the door the original brass plaque, which is the only piece anyone likes.

The crest. The building's house crest exists in exactly two places. It is engraved on that brass plaque, which we photographed on the wall, and it is printed on a letterhead from the fifties that a former tenant found in a filing cabinet, which we scanned. There is no drawing, no plate and no file, and the original architect's practice closed in 1961. We need the crest back as artwork, and it has to be the building's crest and not a designer's impression of it.

The programme. Our fabricator engraves brass and needs artwork he can put on the machine, not a picture. Beyond that we need the entrance sign, a tenant directory board carrying all fourteen suites, and a plate for every suite, all at the sizes in the sign shop's survey, all clearly one family, and delivered so we can change a tenant name ourselves when a lease turns over without paying a designer.

We would also like to see the new plaque on the building before we commit, so the board can approve it.

On tone: our tenants are professional firms who chose a building with a stone entrance and brass fittings. Quiet, traditional, generous with space. Nothing that would look at home on a retail park.

Please include a schedule the fabricator can quote from, and tell us anything you found that we should know.
price_band_and_audience: A listed heritage building letting at forty five to seventy five dollars per square foot to law, architecture and accountancy firms, with a board approving the spend. At this tier the programme is engraved brass and stone appropriate metalwork, a serif with real heritage credibility, deep margins, generous clear space around the crest, and a directory that reads as a document rather than as signage. Push down into a budget system and it becomes moulded plastic, a condensed grotesque, tight margins and a loud contrast board, which at this rent reads as neglect and undermines the one asset the tenants pay for. Push up into contemporary luxury and it becomes a minimal sans on a dark monolith, which fights a 1911 stone entrance and reads as a refurbishment a conservation officer would refuse. Either extreme misreads the commission even where every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No drawing, plate or digital file of the crest exists, and the original architect's practice closed in 1961. The crest survives in exactly two places: engraved on the weathered brass entry plaque, photographed on the wall, and printed on a 1950s tenant letterhead, scanned. assets_supplied.name: marchfield_plaque.jpg (5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: The original engraved brass entry plaque photographed on the facade in late afternoon raking light, handheld, the crest filling most of the frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The plaque by the door. This is the crest, on the real thing."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The polished bevel throws a specular ridge sitting brighter than the engraved field, so a graphic level selection takes the ridge as if it were part of the crest, while along the shaded left third the incised line and the brass run to nearly the same value and the wreath does not come back there at all. Neither is apparent on the photograph, which reads as the sharper and more authoritative of the two sources.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_letterhead.jpg (3400 x 4400)
assets_supplied.kind: A flatbed scan of a 1950s tenant letterhead carrying the same crest at about thirty millimetres, one deep ink on cream stock, the sheet foxed at the edges.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A letterhead a tenant found in a filing cabinet. Same crest, much smaller."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: At the size it was printed the ink gained, so two of the crest's interior rules have run into one another and the ribbon's counters have filled, a closure invisible on the sheet and obvious only beside the other candidate. The crest also occupies a small part of a large scan, so what looks like a high resolution source is a small source inside a big file, and nothing downstream may enlarge it.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_facade.jpg (6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the entrance bay taken for the board's approval mockup, the existing plaque in place in a shaded stone reveal.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The entrance, so we can see the new plaque where it will actually go."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: In the shaded reveal the limestone surround and the brass plaque field run to nearly the same value along the left edge, so an automatic isolation of the plaque area reports success, previews convincingly and bites that edge, leaving a crescent of the old engraving and a ragged stone boundary that appears only at full resolution.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_suite_plate_2019.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The previous sign shop's print ready artwork for a single suite plate from the 2019 refit, a genuine press PDF at plate trim, one ink.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The plate artwork from the last refit. It is the only file the old sign shop left us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The suite number and the firm name look like two separate blocks on the page and are one continuous run in the file, so fields have to be reached by position inside a single story rather than frame by frame. It also carries the abandoned 2019 numbering convention in its own text, which no longer matches the schedule, and no bleed can be introduced into anything derived from it.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_schedule.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The managing agent's current tenant schedule: suite number, floor, firm name and lease status, in the order the directory board is to read.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our current schedule. Fourteen suites, in the order we want them on the board."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two suites appear twice, once under their 2019 number and once under the number in use since the renumbering, so the row count is not the suite count. One suite is vacant with an empty firm cell, which merges into a plate carrying a blank line rather than being skipped, and three firm names carry an ampersand while one runs to thirty eight characters.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_sign_survey.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The fabricator's site survey as plain text: entrance sign, directory board and suite plate sizes in millimetres, substrate and fixing for each, and the shop's minimum engraved stroke width at final size.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our fabricator measured and what his machine can hold."

acceptance_bar: The crest is the building's crest, recovered rather than redrawn, and the same crest appears on the plaque artwork, the entrance sign, the directory board, the suite plate header and the mockup with no drift between them.
The crest still reads at the smallest size it reproduces, the suite plate, with its interior holes still open, judged on brass and never on white.

The engraving artwork is a single closed outline with counters present as true holes, a real viewBox, and no opaque field underneath. Artwork that looks correct on screen and routes solid on the machine fails.
No engraved stroke falls below the fabricator's stated minimum at final size. Anything that does is named in the schedule rather than sent to the machine.
Every panel is authored at the surveyed physical size and nothing runs off a panel edge or into the fixing zone the survey names.
The directory board carries every current tenant exactly once, in the schedule's own order, and the reconciliation that produced that list is written down.
The plate run is one press file whose page count equals the reconciled suite count in schedule order, plus a named file per suite, and no plate carries a blank field where a tenant name should be.
Proofs are genuinely at press resolution at trim rather than a screen scale page enlarged to look like one.
The mockup shows the new plaque in place with clean boundaries at full resolution: no crescent of the old engraving, no bitten stone edge, no halo.
One type system across every panel, with the schedule naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The sign document is editable by the managing agent next season: live retypeable text, the crest as real vector shapes, and the source it was built from delivered alongside.
No delivered file exceeds its source pixel dimensions and no returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.
The programme reads as a listed 1911 building at this rent. A system that would look correct on a retail park fails even where every measurement is right.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, where image_vectorize is counted rather than as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs, image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The recovery and everything physical. It levels and neutralises both candidate captures, lifts the crest at incised and at ink level rather than at object level, traces both candidates, performs the vector hygiene the tracer does not do, derives the engraving outline, and prepares the facade frame so the approval mockup can be authored over a clean plaque field. It is also where the two candidate recoveries are judged against each other at real reproduction size.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The sign programme as one native editable document carrying several roots at their true surveyed millimetre sizes, the only surface here that composes free form layout. The crest goes in as inline SVG so it arrives as real editable vector, the directory is authored as a genuine table so each row is a live cell rather than a picture of a list, the facade frame is inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, and every root declares its own canvas so a global override does not collapse the set.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the whole programme and the one place typography is controllable at all. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so a heritage serif for the building's name and a quieter companion for the directory is the agent's own art direction, judged against a listed building let to professional firms. Numeric weights are non standard per family, a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a weight, every name must be laundered into canonical form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it silently falls back.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and variable data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange, document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution
adobe_surfaces.role: The suite plate run, the one genuine record per page job in the programme. The 2019 sign shop's press artwork is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the reconciled schedule is bound to it, and the run is delivered as an ordered press file plus per suite named files with proofs at press resolution. Its interchange export is also the only honest way to know what the converted document contains before promising a mapping.

Persisting the two recovered crest interpretations for the building's board to approve, since this is a decision the managing agent cannot take alone. Vector is not accepted there so flattened proofs at the sizes that matter are what get placed, each call stays inside the twelve placement cap, and a partial success is read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: Panels at fixed physical sizes are authored layout, fourteen plates at one record per page are variable data work, and the crest is raster archaeology. The survey pins the sizes, so nothing here needs the client.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export later.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Handoff discipline, and it matters here because two captures of the same crest will exist in several intermediate states and confusing them is how the wrong candidate ships.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at both crest captures, the facade frame, the plate artwork and the schedule, and read the survey into the terms the artwork will be judged in: what size the crest reproduces at on each panel and what the fabricator's minimum stroke means there.
trajectory.judgement: The plaque photograph is the more authoritative looking source and the letterhead the more even one, and neither impression is evidence. The survey's minimum stroke is the only hard constraint in the commission and has to be carried from here to the end.
trajectory.produces: A triage note per capture and a table of crest reproduction sizes per panel.

trajectory.action: Straighten both captures and neutralise the overall casts, the warm afternoon light on the brass and the cream of the aged stock.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and consumes edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop, and a cast left in place biases every later separation between mark and ground.
trajectory.produces: Levelled, neutralised masters of both candidates with the applied parameters logged.

trajectory.action: Lift the crest from the plaque capture with a prompt naming the incised line's own visual properties rather than the plaque or the wall, take the returned bounds, set polarity and crop from those bounds.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the object returns a plaque shaped rectangle and every downstream step then works on the wrong thing. Polarity before tracing is the difference between a positive crest and a filled block with the crest knocked out of it, and both routes report success.
trajectory.produces: A prepared plate of the crest from the plaque, in correct polarity, with its selection bounds recorded.

trajectory.action: Do the same on the letterhead capture, lifting printed ink off cream stock rather than incision off metal, and crop from its own returned bounds without enlarging anything.
trajectory.judgement: The two substrates need differently worded selections even though the mark is identical, and the letterhead's crest is physically small inside a large scan, so its native scale is the ceiling for everything derived from it.
trajectory.produces: A prepared plate of the crest from the letterhead at its native scale.

trajectory.action: Trace both candidates, inject a viewBox into each, remove the opaque full canvas path the tracer always writes first, and set the two side by side at the sizes from the reproduction table, on brass, beginning with the smallest.
trajectory.judgement: The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the result can be tuned afterwards and every lever lives upstream in the raster preparation. The comparison has to happen at the size the crest is used, on the ground it sits on, and it is made by eye.
trajectory.produces: Two hygienic candidate crests and a reasoned reading of where each one holds and where it does not.

trajectory.action: Derive the engraving artwork from the settled crest as a single closed outline whose counters are present as holes, plus a reversed variant for dark ground, and check every stroke against the fabricator's stated minimum at final size.
trajectory.judgement: Background removal cannot punch an enclosed interior and hands back a solid disc that looks correct until it sits on a colour, so the interior comes from the selection route. A hairline that survives on an entrance sign can fall under the machine's minimum on a suite plate, which makes this a per panel judgement rather than one artwork.
trajectory.produces: Engraving ready geometry, a reversed variant, and a note of any stroke that cannot meet the minimum.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board and place the candidate interpretations as flattened proofs at the sizes that decide the question, staying inside the placement cap and re-sending only what the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: The building's board is approving a heritage decision, so the proofs must be at the sizes where the candidates differ, not at a flattering size. Vector is not accepted here, which is why proofs rather than artwork are placed.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable approval board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Prepare the facade frame for the approval mockup by isolating the existing plaque field and filling it flat, so the new artwork can be authored over a clean field at true scale.
trajectory.judgement: This frame is the thing the building's board will sign off, so it is inspected at full resolution rather than at the scale a preview offers, and the new plaque sits at the size the survey gives rather than at a size that flatters it.
trajectory.produces: A prepared facade frame ready to carry the new plaque at surveyed scale.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole programme.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own art direction, judged against a listed 1911 building let to professional firms. A display cut is reached by its slug and not by a weight, and the numeric weight cannot be inferred from the style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the entrance sign, the directory board, the plaque artwork sheet and the approval mockup, each root declaring its own surveyed millimetre canvas, the crest as inline SVG inside explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, the directory as a real table, the facade frame inlined as image data, and family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A right anchored auto sized wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, an image left as a URL is not an image, and a global canvas parameter collapses a mixed size set. The design work is the restraint the tier demands: how much stone the panels leave, how large the crest sits, how quiet the directory reads.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, and verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first panel, and parse the returned per panel markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas. Looking at panel one is not looking at the programme.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first panel, and a markup audit of the others.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the tenant schedule against the 2019 renumbering, settle the vacant suite, and produce the file that will drive the plate run.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes the schedule is the suite list. A duplicated suite produces two plates for one door and a vacant suite produces a plate with a hole in it, so both are client facing decisions to be made, applied consistently and disclosed.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled run file and a written record of every change made to the agent's data.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2019 plate artwork into a layout document, export its interchange form to see what the file contains, build the mapping against the frames that exist, validate it, prepare the template, then re-export the interchange form and read which placeholders are really there.
trajectory.judgement: Identifiers are integer item ids rather than interchange strings, the mapping travels as one stringified object, wholesale text replacement is rejected by validation so targeted replacement is the workhorse, and a success message about placeholder creation is not evidence that a placeholder exists.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template and a placeholder by placeholder reading of what it contains.

trajectory.action: Merge the reconciled schedule into the template and render the run off the merged document: the ordered press file, per suite named files, and fabricator proofs at press resolution at trim.
trajectory.judgement: Resolution asked for at merge time is silently ignored, so real resolution comes only from rendering the merged document, and identity is guaranteed by the ordered document or a single record loop, never by the position of a file in a response.
trajectory.produces: An ordered plate press file, a named per suite set, and press resolution proofs.

trajectory.action: Write the signage schedule the fabricator can quote from and the note the managing agent asked for, covering panels, substrates, sizes, crest reproduction size per panel, minimum stroke exceptions, the schedule reconciliation and the type system by role.
trajectory.judgement: The schedule is a working document for a tradesman and the note is for a managing agent, and they are not the same document. Both have to name what could not be done as plainly as what could.
trajectory.produces: A fabricator ready schedule sheet and a written handover note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the two surviving records of the crest is usable, and the answer is that neither is usable whole. The plaque photograph is larger, sharper and the real object, but the raking light's specular ridge along the bevel traces as if it were geometry and the shaded left third gives no separation at all, so the wreath is simply absent there. The letterhead is even and complete but was printed small, so the ink gained until two interior rules merged and the ribbon's counters filled, a closure invisible on the sheet that declares itself only beside the other trace at suite plate size. Both traces succeed, both look convincing at canvas scale, and the failures are in different places on each.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not avoid it, and tracing both is competent practice rather than a dodge, because what cannot be known in advance is where each source fails, which is a property of this light on this metal and this ink on this stock. The tracer has no parameters at all. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the crest survives in two places and must come back as the building's crest. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain: a confined correction over the shaded third to open a separation that does not yet exist, a re-worded selection at incised level, a re-trace, and a fresh comparison at the same reproduction sizes.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster stage on the chosen capture, lift the shaded region with a confined correction rather than a whole frame move, re-select and re-trace, and judge the result again at the smallest reproduction size on brass before anything downstream is built on it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A heritage crest shipped to a brass engraver with a specular ridge cut into it as if it were part of the design, or with a wreath that stops a third of the way round, permanently, on a listed building's entrance.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the treatment the whole programme's look rests on. An incised, engraved register is reached in an authored page by exactly the constructions this importer quietly discards: a blur filter is dropped outright, a layered shadow is truncated to its first layer, a text shadow is dropped, an outline is dropped, and a stroked letterform written with a text stroke and a transparent fill comes back fully invisible rather than as an outline. Every one of those returns success with no warning. The document's own rendition shows the first panel only, so the entrance sign may look right while the directory board and the plate sheet have lost the treatment entirely, and the returned per panel markup is the only channel that reports it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time would mean knowing in advance which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which nothing reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a quiet traditional register and for panels the agent can edit later. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction: the incised register rebuilt from what does survive, real strokes on shapes, a single shadow layer, borders and gradients, or carried up into the raster stage so the treatment is part of the artwork rather than a page effect, then a re-author and a fresh audit of every panel.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the incised treatment from constructions the importer keeps, re-author the HTML around that decision, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every panel from the returned markup rather than from the first one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A sign programme approved by a building's board on the strength of the one panel anybody looked at, with the directory board and the plate sheet arriving flat, and in the worst case a panel whose lettering is present in the document and invisible on the canvas.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the plaque field in the facade photograph can be isolated cleanly at all. In the shaded reveal the limestone surround and the brass run to nearly the same value along the left edge, and an automatic isolation there returns a result that reports success, previews convincingly at the scale anyone would check it at, and bites that edge, so a crescent of the old engraving survives inside the supposedly cleared field and the stone boundary comes back ragged. Where it bites, and how far, is a property of this bay in this light and appears only at full resolution.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the tool has no edge tolerance to set and the failure is in the material rather than in the call. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only to see the new plaque on the building before the board commits. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain: select the limestone as a material by its own surface properties, invert that selection, and drive the fill from the ground instead of from the object, a route the naive attempt never touches.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the object led isolation, select the surrounding stone as a material, invert it, fill from that mask, and inspect the boundary at full resolution rather than at preview scale before the mockup panel is authored around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An approval mockup in which the old engraving is still faintly visible under the new plaque and the stone edge is chewed, put in front of a building's board as the thing they are asked to sign off.

deliverables.name: Recovered Marchfield crest and engraving geometry
deliverables.spec: The house crest recovered from physical survivors rather than redrawn, as placeable scalable artwork with a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas path underneath, delivered as the master, a reversed variant for dark ground, and an engraving ready single closed outline whose counters are true holes. Every stroke at or above the fabricator's stated minimum at each panel's own reproduction size, with any exception named rather than shipped.

deliverables.name: Marchfield sign programme: entrance sign, directory board, plaque sheet and approval mockup
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying each panel as its own root at its surveyed physical size, with live retypeable text in one licensed type system, the crest present as real vector shapes rather than a picture, the directory as a genuine table so a tenant row can be edited in place when a lease turns over, and the approval mockup carrying the prepared facade frame with the new plaque at true scale. Delivered with the self contained source, which is the durable half.

deliverables.name: Suite plate run, press file and per suite set
deliverables.spec: The 2019 sign shop's press artwork reverse engineered into a live merge template bound to the reconciled schedule, delivered as one press file whose page count equals the reconciled suite count in schedule order, plus per suite named files with identity guaranteed rather than inferred from output position, plus fabricator proofs at press resolution at trim. No plate carries a blank field and no suite appears twice.

deliverables.name: Fabricator schedule and handover note
deliverables.spec: A signage schedule the fabricator can quote from, listing every panel with its size, substrate, fixing, finish and the crest's reproduction size on it, plus a separate written note for the managing agent recording which capture each element of the crest came from and why, the parameters applied at each stage, every change made to the tenant schedule, the type system by role with family, foundry and actual weight, and every limit found, including what cannot be introduced into artwork derived from the 2019 file.

verifiers_auto.text: The delivered crest and the engraving outline carry a viewBox and no full canvas opaque path at index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse each delivered SVG, assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The engraving artwork's counters exist as real interior subpaths rather than as painted shapes.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the outline's path data for interior subpaths and check the fill rule that makes them read as holes.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are authored panels at fixed physical sizes and which is a genuine record per page run, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which surviving record of the crest is the master, when the more authoritative looking capture is not necessarily the more even one and the answer may be neither on its own.

Selection wording per substrate: incision in brass and printed ink on aged stock need different prompts even though the mark is identical, and naming the object returns the plaque or the sheet instead of the crest.
How much of the crest's detail survives at suite plate size, and whether a simplified interpretation is needed below a stated size or whether one drawing serves every panel.
How to produce true interior holes, given that background removal fills an enclosed interior and returns something that looks correct until it sits on a colour.
What the fabricator's minimum stroke means per panel, since a hairline that is fine on an entrance sign can be unroutable on a plate.
Which incised register to build the panels out of, once the difference between what a page can express and what survives an import is known.
How to reconcile a tenant schedule the client believes is the suite list, given a renumbering that left duplicates and a vacant suite that would otherwise print a plate with a hole in it.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a listed 1911 building at forty five to seventy five dollars a square foot rather than against a signage category.
How to deliver identity safely across fourteen plates, since files named by their position in a response are not files named by whose door they go on.
How much space the panels give away. At this tier generosity is the design, and a dense, information packed board is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome heraldic crest and pictures of signs. IDENTITY: this is a specific 1911 building's own crest, surviving on two physical objects, and a regenerated crest is a different building's history, which is exactly what a listed building's board is paying not to receive. SPEC: the fabricator engraves from geometry, so the deliverable is a closed outline with true interior holes whose every stroke clears his machine's stated minimum at each panel's real size, and the plates are a page per suite in the agent's own schedule order carrying real tenant names at press resolution at trim, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the whole point of the handover is that the agent changes a tenant name themselves when a lease turns over, so the directory has to be live cells and the plate template has to be re-runnable. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: which capture holds where, whether this counter is still a hole at plate size, whether the isolation bit the stone, whether the treatment survived on the panels nobody previewed.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces counted honestly with image_vectorize counted as imaging and no dead surface used. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, including a pixel accurate stroke only selection of a printed mark on a photographed object with counters correctly excluded, a clean multi path trace that kept strokes rather than returning a silhouette, and material level selection of a surface by prompt (a 672,398 px mask of a painted wood field). The checkpoints rest on live findings: prompt wording is the entire gate and naming the substrate returns the substrate at full success; vectorize takes no options at all; remove_background returns a solid opaque disc on an enclosed interior (118,823 opaque px where a true knockout would have been about 18,000); and the importer drops filter blur, text shadow and outline outright, truncates multi layer shadow to layer one, and renders a text stroke with transparent fill as fully invisible, all at HTTP success. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, exact physical canvases at 96 dpi (210 by 297 mm resolving to 794 by 1123 px), inline SVG becoming native editable vector, real tables with per cell text and strokes, and a genuine editable document are verified, the rendition preview is first canvas only, and photographs must be inlined as image data because every external URL resolved to a placeholder. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, with case sensitivity, non standard numeric weights, display cuts reached by slug and one bad name killing the kit all live findings. INDESIGN: convert, idml, mapping, prepare, merge, render is verified end to end, one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page count equal to row count, per record identity is guaranteed by createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, and 300 dpi at trim comes from the render. BOARDS: persistence, the twelve placement cap, partial success at 201 and no vector are verified. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no upscaling, no compositing, no object removal, no OCR, no text to image, no generative call of any kind, no bleed claim on a converted template, no named press preset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
